dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: This book... goes here, and then this one... Where does this one go?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Hmm... This one's pretty boring — how about I put it way down here?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Ah! Now this one, this one's much more interesting... Yes, let's make sure we put it within easy reach.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Come on, brain, move it! Speed things up! We can't keep Lady Lauma waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you ready to record the story?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Not yet. Every time I think about recording Lady Lauma's "anecdotes," my brain freezes up. It's like I lose the ability to think.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: What should I ask? No, that's not right — how can I ask anything? I just need to listen...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: No, that's not right either! All of the previous recorders asked questions. If I don't ask any, it'll seem like I'm not taking the task seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see you have things to think over. Goodbye...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Come on, brain, hop to it! Get moving!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just think of it as listening to a story.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: That's easy enough to say, but I can't help getting nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: *sigh* I think I'm starting to understand why all the previous recorders wrote like they were penning accounting reports.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Faced with someone so important telling stories so significant, they didn't dare add any embellishments at all.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Taking down a record without mistakes or omissions is already a momentous task...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But you want to make it interesting, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: I should've slapped myself... No, a slap isn't nearly enough — I wish I'd stuffed my fist in my mouth to prevent me from saying a thing back then.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: That way, I wouldn't be stuck pulling my hair out, unable to write down a single word.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: O Moon Goddess... Save me!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Come on, brain, move it! Speed things up! We can't keep Lady Lauma and Lady Columbina waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you ready to record the story?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Not yet. Every time I think about recording Lady Lauma's "anecdotes" and Lady Columbina's "kuuhenki stories," my brain freezes up. It's like I lose the ability to think.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: What should I ask? No, that's not right — how can I ask anything? I just need to listen...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: No, that's not right either! All of the previous Notetakers asked questions. If I don't ask any, it'll seem like I'm not taking the task seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Wait, even the Moon Goddess can't save me now. Lady Columbina is my interview subject too!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: *sob*... What should I do...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (<color=#FFCC33FF>Columbina</color> seems interested...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: You still haven't decided on a title for your book?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Whoa...! You... no, forgive me... Lady Kuutar!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I am Columbina Hyposelenia.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Ah! I—I Never imagined I'd bump into Lady Kuutar...!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Right, right...! I can ask her about the Moonchanters!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Umm... Lady Columbina, please, please, please... Could you please do me a favor?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Well... you know the Moonchanter, right? Could you... could you tell me some funny or interesting stories about them?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I know of them. But I only know how they look when they pray.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Their prayers aren't very interesting, and I'm sure Lauma knows the words just as well.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: I see... *sigh* Then what am I supposed to put at the start of Lost Tales of the Moonchanters? I can't really open with Lady Lauma's stories, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "Lost Tales of the Moonchanters"?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's a little collection I wanted to write... and the title was Lady Lauma's idea.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: She said, "a book that presents those tales in an interesting and humorous manner could go a long way to inspiring interest in history amongst the children."

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: "And this interest may then guide them to undertake more serious historical research later down the line."

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Ugh... so embarrassing! Why was I mumbling to myself out here?! Lady Lauma overheard everything and caught me right on the spot!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: And then she said, "I have faith in you. You have not spent much time as a priestess, but you are no one's inferior in wisdom or texts studied."

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: "I believe you are more than up to the task of composing such a text."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Lauma meant that you're very capable.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh... maybe? No, no, I'm not! I... I haven't even found the very first story...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I don't know stories about the Moonchanters, but I do know a few about the kuuhenki. Would you like to hear them?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: W—Would you really? Err, um, pl—please wait one moment, Lady Columbina! I haven't any paper or pen on hand, and I'm n—not mentally prepared either! Could you... tell me the story later...?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: All right. Next time I come by to eat some fruit, I'll come find you.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Yes! Of course! No problem at all, Lady Columbina!

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: ...Though "next time I come by to eat fruit?" What kind of timekeeping is that...?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Hmm, where should this book go...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}? Welcome! Lady Lauma mentioned you.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: That said, if you're looking for her, you'll have to wait a bit — she just went out to attend to some business.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you organizing the books?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: That I am. Since this library was built, Lady Lauma has asked us to shift as much of our book collection in as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: And then... She also requested that we make some cushions and stands for the animals...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: She said that this would give them a place to rest when they visit.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: I don't really understand it, but she must have her reasons for giving such instructions.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Alright. We'll just put this book — and boy, is it thick as a brick — on the bottom-most shelf. That way, anyone who wants to use it as a footrest or stool just needs to pull it out.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Oh, don't worry, this is a running account of the words and deeds Moonchanters over various generations. It's in manuscript form, too...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: *sigh* And yes, I know that I shouldn't be saying this as a priestess, but this book is... likely the least interesting in this entire library.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: It's just... "on such and such a day, month, and year, Moonchanter A said this and did that, and these were the results or consequences" all the way down.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: I would flip through its pages every time sleep eluded me, and it worked like a charm every time.

choices.text: Is there nothing interesting in it at all?

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: ...Well, they exist, just not in that book. I have heard quite a good many such tales, though. I don't have this job for nothing, you know. Hehe.

choices.text: Err, is that really a priestess's job?

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: From my sister priestesses, of course! They know all sorts of stories, let me tell you.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: For example, one of our previous Moonchanters had a strange habit of spending two hours soaking in a nearby lake whenever she had to organize some ceremony, regardless of the season.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: She would say that the lake reflected the moon, and that she could enjoy the favor of its light and goddess while thusly immersed, which would then help the ceremony proceed smoothly.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: In times where a great many ceremonies were held, she would be soaking practically every day...

choices.text: Those ceremonies went off without a wrinkle, then...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Oh, absolutely, and she was a most capable Moonchanter. But...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: The long-term exposure to cold caused that devout Moonchanter to develop a serious case of arthritis, which forced her to bow out early...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: But despite that premature retirement, she maintained that the pain was a mark of the Moon Goddess's regard...

choices.text: I don't think the Moon Goddess's dominions cover arthritis...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Well... The moon would be covered by the clouds and disappear when it would rain. She believed that the accompanying joint pains were the Moon Goddess bidding her farewell.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And if the moon could be seen even in such times?

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Then it was the Moon Goddess's summons. She would run out into the rain, fully clothed, and begin to pray...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Later, in her old age, we had to find her an acolyte to watch her permanently and ensure that she did not risk her health further.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: And that lucky prie— Whoops, no, that fortunate acolyte... That was me.

choices.text: No wonder you know all these stories.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Hehe, of course. I wasn't just listening to her stories, though. I learned much as well.

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: If I get the chance in future, I'll write them all down in a book. Then I'll call it...

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Oh! Oh dear, oh dear, too much chatting, not enough book-sorting. Still... Hmm. What should I call that book...

choices.text: It seems your time as an acolyte paid off, then.
How are these two related, precisely?
Could her body really hold up under all that?

response.speaker: Ehrnrooth
response.text: Haha... The ceremonies she organized went well, at least. But...

choices.text: And where did you hear these tales, I wonder...
I'd have thought there'd be some interesting anecdotes in there...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Frostmoon Scions' history...)

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: (Ehrnrooth started talking to herself, but she seems stuck on the book name...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perhaps someone familiar with the Scions' history could help her pick a suitable one...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (<color=#FFCC33FF>Lauma</color> seems interested...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: If I get the chance in future, I'll write them all down in a book. Then I'll call it...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Oh! Oh dear, oh dear, too much chatting, not enough book-sorting. Still... Hmm. What should I call that book...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: How about... "Lost Tales of the Moonchanters"?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Ah! L—L—Lady Lauma! I—I, uh, I— I didn't mean to... Well, I guess I did mean to...

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: S—S—Sorry, I'll stop with the nonsense now!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Pfft. You misunderstand. I'm not angry. I was serious about that name.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I had this library built precisely to better record our history, such that those who come after us have records they may consult.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And if one were to tell our history, it would be remiss of us to not speak of the Moonchanters.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yet... the texts that tell their tales are either challenging and cryptic, or as hefty as they are humdrum.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Never mind you. Even I... *chuckle* Let's just say I've had to exercise much patience and perseverance in trudging through them.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: W—W—Wait, so you heard everything I said? I, well, they're actually not that hard to read. Just a couple pages a day, and boom, you're done before you know it. I mean, I've done it. Honest...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Even so, it might be a tall order to expect people to read in this way and still retain the information for any length of time.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You said that you wanted to write down those stories about the Moonchanters into a compilation. I think that's a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: A book that presents those tales in an interesting and humorous manner could go a long way to inspiring interest in history amongst the children.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And this interest may then guide them to undertake more serious historical research later down the line.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Still, this task will be far from easy, Ehrnrooth. Would you be willing to help me?

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: O—O—Of course I can... Well, err, I might...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I have faith in you. You have not spent much time as a priestess, but you are no one's inferior in wisdom or texts studied.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I believe you are more than up to the task of composing such a text.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: I... I'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'll leave it to you, then. Hmm... As the current Moonchanter, allow me to share a story with you as well.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: W—Would you really? Err, um, pl—please wait one moment, Lady Lauma! I haven't any paper or pen on hand, and I'm n—not mentally prepared either! Could you... tell me the story later...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Of course. Just come to see me once your preparations are complete. I'll make myself available.

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Yes, Lady Lauma!
